NgraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale:
The maintainer ruled that payments are recorded as historical rows written directly into registry.xml. Archived specs are never edited. That ruling is implemented, not reopened.
kind="historical" is the honest member. The derivation currently sees only kind="chartered" (scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:731). Reusing chartered would make the rows visible with no code change, and would say these bundles were chartered in advance in this registry. They were not. A closed union that lies about its members turns eligibility — D28.1's enforcement — into a formality, which is the defect this bundle exists to refuse in the payment itself. kind="sweep-remainder" is the leftover-name table with empty Pays; stuffing tokens there would be a second lie and would stay invisible. Widening the union and the filter, and erroring on any other kind value, is the product change that makes the new member real.
The brief asked what StatusText must say because collectPaidBy allegedly requires /delivered|superseded/i. That predicate is not in the shipped function. It is staged F180's description of collectPaidBy at 67bc55c (:372-410), before C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY widened the derivation to Closed with and the archived-spec payer phrase. A finding is never evidence of present state. Historical StatusText still has to be true — **Delivered**, because the four bundles are archived applied — but it is not a gate on the payer map. The AC-KIND-VISIBLE fixture uses a StatusText that does not match that regex so the probe cannot pass by accidentally depending on it.
F90+F90.1+F35 wrap 249, which cleared the brief's 494-line staged wrap by 7 under a 252+Delta window. The buffer is untracked and has grown: 17 findings wrap 609 under the F181 / parseFrozenMarkdown bodyRaw-plus-3 rule. 249 no longer clears it. F27 and F38 are required fuel, not margin. F27.1 and F27.2 ride the same C-DECLARED-WRITES row, already required for F27, and were verified against the same witnesses; they restore margin without a fifth row and without a ceiling question.

Alternatives.Alternative: Reuse kind="chartered". No union change; the filter already sees the row. Rejected: semantically false, and it teaches the next author that kind is decorative.
Add kind="historical" without widening the filter. The rows exist and remain invisible. Rejected: inert, which is the current defect in a new costume.

Write the rows directly into registry-retired.xml. Live occupancy never moves; ceiling cannot breach. Rejected: the maintainer ruled the rows are written into registry.xml; AC- CEILING-ORDER's before-retire observation exists to keep that ruling testable.
Edit the four archived specs to carry the payer phrase. No new kind. Rejected: archived bundles are never edited.
Pay only F90, F90.1, and F35, as the brief's minimum. Rejected at this HEAD: 249 < 357, so the flush stays blocked. Not a deferral of F27 / F38 — those witnesses were already verified.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: None. D11: F90.1 residuals, F35.1, and F36 are out because they lack a verified present-tree witness for this payment set, not because they were filed for later.

Scenarios.Scenario: Executor widens the union and the filter, adds the four rows to live registry.xml, runs --retire, then commits. validate:ci sees live occupancy 11, four historical rows in the retired sibling, seven tokens retired with stamped PaidBy, exit 0.
Executor commits the four live rows without --retire. validate:ci fails on registry-eligible-still- live and finding-eligible-still- live. That commit is not a deliverable of this bundle.
A later author writes kind="Historical" or kind="history". Validate errors rather than dropping the row from the payer map.
